subject: Three-way latency & throughput sweep — next tests and owners
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Three-way latency & throughput sweep — next tests and owners

Sanjay / team — great meeting today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next tests so we can qualify the p95/p99 and tokens/sec deltas you saw in the demo.

Summary of ask from Quantix: confirm whether the latency delta (~40–60ms p95) against their current Hyperscaler+API is material under their workload, and validate throughput (tokens/sec) at sustained concurrency for the two model sizes.

Proposed three-way sweep (short):
- Variant A: Redwood hosted, model: rw-medium-quantized (customer baseline in demo).
- Variant B: Hyperscaler A (HyperCloud managed endpoint) — customer-provided region + config we saw in demo.
- Variant C: Hyperscaler B (MegaCloud) / or their internal self-host (if they want) — capture both if possible.

Test matrix (attached spreadsheet):
- Payload profiles: short (prompt ~40 tokens), medium (~180 tokens), long (~600 tokens) — see payload-samples.jsonl.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (sustained over 5m windows), cold-start 30s, cache-hit vs no-cache.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16 simult.
- Warm vs cold: run 3 warm runs before capture; capture final run for publication.

Critical gating questions we need to answer during the sweep:
1) Is the p95 delta stable across medium+long payloads or does it grow with sequence length?
2) At what concurrency point does tokens/sec or p99 degrade >2x relative to baseline?
3) Any variance in cold-starts or KV cache behavior that explains demo difference?

Owners / asks (quick):
- Ben: own Redwood run (Variant A) + attach run configs and raw logs (Raw format + summary).
- Karthik: coordinate Hyperscaler A config confirmation and MegaCloud contact details.
- Evelyn: log the customer-side acceptance criteria (what delta would be considered a blocker vs acceptable).
- Sanjay: confirm if you want us to run Variant C (self-host) or if we should contact MegaCloud instead.

Attachments: quantix-bench-plan.xlsx, payload-samples.jsonl.

Timeline: propose 48–72 hour runway to execute the sweep once we have Hyperscaler configs — aiming for a readout next Tuesday.

If that works, I’ll schedule a quick sync for Friday morning to lock configs.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: quantix-bench-plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantix.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Three-way latency & throughput sweep — next tests and owners

Thanks Vanessa — I can run Variant A. Quick notes on config to keep results clean:
- Model tokenization: use quantized weights but identical tokenizer across runs.
- Ensure KV cache enabled for medium/long runs — but capture a run with KV disabled for apples-to-apples.
- Measure p99 both with and without batching; Redwood continuous batching will be disabled for baseline capture, then re-enabled to show optimization delta.

I’ll upload run configs + a short script that produces the summary CSV to the Drive link. Expect raw logs + summary by EOD Friday.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: raw-logs-snippet.txt (text/plain)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantix.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Three-way latency & throughput sweep — next tests and owners

Looping in the Hyperscaler ops contact I used in the demo (I have the contact on file). For clarity: we should capture the exact endpoint config used in Quantix demo (VM size, instance type, auto-scaler policy, max concurrency, quantization flags). I’ll confirm HyperCloud settings by EOD.

Notes for Variant B/C runs:
- We should request a single-threaded and multi-threaded config snapshot from each hyperscaler; differences in thread scheduling and kernel selection often explain small deltas at p95.
- For fairness, run each variant in the same region (US-West) and with the same network egress path when possible.
- Add a short synthetic microburst test (20 requests in 500ms) to capture microburst p99 behavior.

I’ll post hyperscaler config confirmation to the Drive link when I have it.

Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantix.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, procurement@quantix.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Sep 2029 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Three-way latency & throughput sweep — next tests and owners

Thanks — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side before you run: 
- Please include a token-budgeted conversation profile (our primary product uses ~220 tokens avg per request; we can provide rolling samples if helpful).
- For Variant C: please run MegaCloud (we do not want to share self-hosted configs yet).
- Our acceptance criteria: p95 within 1.2x of our current Hyperscaler A is preferred; p99 should not regress more than 1.5x during sustained concurrency.

We’ll send an S3 link with 1,000 sample prompts (220 tokens avg) by EOD. Happy for Redwood to proceed with runs once HyperCloud config is confirmed by Karthik.

— Sanjay
Head of ML Ops, Quantix AI
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantix.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Sep 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Three-way latency & throughput sweep — next tests and owners

Received, thanks Sanjay. Action plan:
- Karthik to post HyperCloud config by EOD Fri; Ben to run Redwood Variant A and upload logs by EOD Fri.
- Ben & Karthik to coordinate on the microburst and cold-start scripts so tests are identical.
- Evelyn to capture Quantix acceptance criteria into the deal record and confirm the evaluation window.
- Once we have your S3 sample prompts we’ll run the medium/long/short sweep and share the p95/p99 and tokens/sec CSVs + short executive one-pager.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute readout slot for Tue 17 Sep 2029 at 9:00am PT — tentative, I’ll send the invite once we have artifacts.

Thanks all — will update the HubSpot deal with the attachments and status.

Vanessa Ortiz
